mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market discounts the lower discount rate for future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures (each falling > 1% in the past month) indicate a severe demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 1% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 1% in the past month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), higher interest rates increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (indicating robust manufacturing and supply chain activity) signals strong economic growth, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL rising > 0.5% in one month) signals potential monetary tightening, increasing uncertainty and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in non-farm payrolls and increases in the unemployment rate (each exceeding 0.3% in the past month) indicate a severe labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 0.3% and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS declines > 0.3% and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in the past month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle contraction regimes (INDPRO < 100), declining industrial output signals weakening economic activity, reducing corporate profits and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
